chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There was a man among the Children of Israel who supplicated to Allah that He grant him a son for three years. When he saw that Allah was not answering him, he said, 'O Lord! Am I far from You, so You do not hear me, or are You close to me, so You do not answer me?'

He said: So a visitor came to him in his dream and said, 'You have been supplicating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for three years with an obscene tongue, an arrogant heart that is not pious, and an intention that is not sincere. So desist from your obscenities, let your heart fear Allah, and let your intention be improved.'
He said: So the man did that, then supplicated to Allah, and a son was born to him.
ai.seo_question: Why was a man's supplication for a son rejected for three years according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under 'The Obscenities,' this hadith illustrates the Shia principle that the efficacy of *dua* depends not only on the request but on the spiritual purity of the supplicant. The rejection is attributed to a triad of defects: an obscene tongue (*lisan*), an arrogant heart (*qalb*), and insincere intention (*niyyah*), highlighting that internal states directly influence divine response. This narrative serves as a practical guide for believers to examine their character and sincerity before seeking divine favor.
